newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian rocket, satellite explode at launch.
newsitem.headline: Russian rocket, satellite explode at launch.

text.p: A Russian rocket carrying a military satellite smashed to earth and burned on Tuesday seconds after it was launched from the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, a spokesman for the Military-Space Forces agency said.

He said the crash occurred after the engines in the first stage of the Ukrainian-made Zenit-2 booster rocket switched off inexplicably. The rocket went down in the steppe near Baikonur. Nobody was hurt.
"The two-stage booster crashed from an altitude of 15 km (nine miles) 48 seconds after the take-off," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
"The rocket crashed 28 km (15 miles) from the launch site, setting off a very strong explosion and a fire. Nobody was hurt... People participating in the launch were in a shelter."
Military Space Forces set up a commission to investigate the cause of the crash, and the spokesman said there would be no new Zenit launches until the panel had reached a conclusion.

Itar-Tass news agency said it was the first Zenit-2 launch this year and the seventh case of malfunction since Russia started launching them in 1985. Russia has launched 28 Zenit-2 rockets, lifting 22 satellites, mostly military.

An upgraded three-stage version of Zenit-2 will be used to launch commercial satellites from the Pacific Ocean under the international Sea Launch project involving the United States, Norway, Ukraine and Russia.
